question: Every Member State in the euro area has a duty to respect basic obligations of budgetary discipline when conducting its economic policy, in accordance with the existing institutional framework. Compliance with this framework is achieved with technical support from various national bodies, such as the budget offices and the courts of auditors.

At the same time, however, the drawing up of the budget is a leading expression of national sovereignty and democratic debate. Hence, opposition parties are also involved in the process of voting national budgets. However, so far there is no institutional framework in place to give them access to technical support when drawing up their own policy proposals.

The resulting risk is the expression of opinions which deviate from the existing budgetary discipline framework, and the spread of unsubstantiated and dangerous opinions in European societies. In the light of this uneven access to technical support during the process of formulating economic policies, can the Commission say: 1.

Is it prepared to introduce an obligation for Member States to provide technical support to political parties outside government in order to draft political proposals that comply with the existing budgetary discipline framework?
Is it prepared to introduce mechanisms for providing independent information to citizens on the content of the budgets voted on by the Member States?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (29.6.2026) 1. Based on proposals of the Commission, the position of independent fiscal institutions in each Member State was significantly strengthened in the 2024 review of European economic governance1. The independent fiscal institutions bring clarity and improve transparency in the national debate on public finances.

For example, one of their tasks, according to Article 8a(5) of Council Directive 2011/85/EU2, is to participate in hearings of national parliaments. Member States had until the end of 2025 to transpose the corresponding amendments into national law and the Commission is currently assessing the transposition.

The Commission shall publish a review of the effectiveness of this Directive by 31 December 2030 and, at the same time, shall also report on the capacity and tasks of independent fiscal institutions. 2.

Providing independent information on the content of budgets to the general public is one of the core activities of the independent fiscal institutions in Member States whose institutional role was codified and strengthened by Directive 2011/85/EU on requirements for budgetary frameworks of the Member States.
